rule: Every number in wtc1.glb and wtc2.glb comes from a parameter listed under `params`, by id. Nothing was estimated, scaled, rounded or averaged. Floors and members with no cited dimension are listed under each building's `omitted`.
paradata_file: data/paradata.json (P-030 to P-046) and data/paradata.exterior.json (P-060 onward, facade decisions)

units.conversion: 1 ft = 0.3048 m and 1 ft = 12 in, exactly. Source values are feet or inches as recorded per param.

frame.origin: centre of the column-reference-line square in plan; y = 0 at the floor 1 (Concourse) line, param towers.floor_1_elevation
frame.elevations: elevation_ft on each node is the drawing datum of NCSTAR 1-1 Figure 2-2 / 2-3 (Concourse = 310 ft), not sea level
frame.tower_positions: unresolved (complex.tower_positions_and_spacing): each file is in its own local frame; the viewer places the two towers

node_naming.floor_plate: <building>_floor_<NNN>  (three-digit floor number, e.g. wtc1_floor_042); one thin box per cited floor line, top face on the floor line
node_naming.sublevel_plate: <building>_sublevel_<n> and <building>_service_level, labelled per the NCSTAR 1-2A drawing index (B1 in Table G-1 = service level EL. 294; see P-042)
node_naming.core_segment: <building>_core_<key>  (one centred box between consecutive cited lines; key is the three-digit floor at the bottom of the segment, e.g. wtc1_core_042, or the sub-level label below grade, e.g. wtc1_core_sublevel_5)
node_naming.column_story: <building>_columns_<NNN>  (one EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing node per story from the floor NNN line to the next cited floor line, 236 instances each; instances are not individually named)
node_naming.spandrel_line: <building>_spandrels_<NNN>  (one EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing node per column line 9 to 107, 4 instances: one 52 in. deep box per face centred on the floor line; P-060)
node_naming.glass_story: <building>_glass_<NNN>  (one EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing node per story 9 to 107, 232 quads: one per bay per face, standing on the column reference line between spandrels; P-061)
node_naming.detail_nodes: core_<NNN>, columns_<NNN>, spandrels_<NNN> and glass_<NNN> match parseDetailNodeName() in lib/geometry-naming.ts, so the viewer can hide them per floor on a reduced tier
node_naming.materials: plate, core, column_cladding, spandrel_cladding, glass (named; the viewer replaces plate materials per floor). Cladding and infill materials are cited (towers.exterior_cladding_material, towers.window_infill); the colours are rendering choices, P-062.

derived.note: The glass quads are this wide. It is the clear gap between steel column faces, computed here from two cited values; the window width itself is unresolved (towers.window_width) and the visible opening was narrower because the aluminum column covers were wider than the steel (towers.spandrel_cover_and_cladding_dimensions, unresolved). Paradata P-061.

pipeline.compression: EXT_meshopt_compression, method QUANTIZE, encoded with meshoptimizer's MeshoptEncoder (no quantize() pass, so every value is the float32 the generator computed). Draco is not used.
pipeline.gltfpack: not run. gltfpack rewrites EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing input into one unnamed node per mesh at the scene root regardless of -kn / -mi (verified 2026-09-11), which would drop the per-story wtc1_columns_NNN nodes the viewer hides per floor. Use it later for KTX2 (-tc) on textured assets that carry no instancing.
pipeline.verification: compressed files are read back with the meshopt decoder; node names, triangle and instance counts, and every named node's POSITION / TRANSLATION array must match the uncompressed file exactly

nodes.name: wtc1_columns_009
nodes.note: EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing: one box per column per story, 59 per face at 3 ft 4 in. on centre starting 6 ft 11 in. from each column reference line; a story spanning an undivided dimension (41 to 43) is one taller box. Cladding projection and corner members are not modelled (see spandrels and glass nodes for the infill).

nodes.name: wtc1_spandrels_009
nodes.note: One box per face, 52 in. deep, centred vertically on the cited floor line; length 193 ft 4 in. plus one 14 in. column width; depth equals the column depth so the cladding reads as one surface. Plate thickness and cladding projection are not modelled.

nodes.name: wtc1_glass_009

Height is the story minus the 52 in. spandrel. The quad stands on the column reference line.

unresolved_relevant.why: NCSTAR 1-1 says only that 'the window openings were infilled with glass fitted into aluminum frames and sealed with neoprene gaskets' (pdf p70). No clear width between column faces, sill height, or head height is stated; the 40 in. on-center pitch and 14 in. approximate column width are stated separately and subtracting them is an inference this file does not make.
unresolved_relevant.where_to_look: NCSTAR 1-1A (architectural design documents); NCSTAR 1-5A (window breakage modeling states window dimensions); NCSTAR 1-3 (exterior column plate dimensions per panel). None of 1-1A / 1-5A were fetchable from the nvlpubs Legacy path on 2026-09-10 (404).

unresolved_relevant.why: Figure 2-2 (the only story-by-story schedule in NCSTAR 1-1) is the west elevation of WTC 1. NCSTAR 1-2A states WTC 2 was 1,362 ft, 6 ft shorter, so at least one interval differs, but neither report itemizes the WTC 2 stories. Searched again 2026-09-11 for the generator: the Tower B structural steel drawing index (NCSTAR 1-2A pdf p189-p191) lists framing plans by floor number with no elevation above floor 1; Table G-1 (pdf p224) lists floor usage and construction type without elevations; Figure 3-4 (WTC 2 model elevation, pdf p33) letters no elevations; the only WTC 2 height statement in either report is 1,362 ft (1-2A pdf p34) and NCSTAR 1-1 pdf p71 says only '6 ft taller than WTC 2'. MODELED MEANWHILE under the P-046 assumption (12 ft typical, evidence reported) per Chris Cousins 2026-09-11; a found schedule replaces wtc2.height_fl2_to_fl110 and wtc2.height_fl110_to_roof.
unresolved_relevant.where_to_look: NCSTAR 1-2 Chapter 2; NCSTAR 1-2A Appendix C drawing books (Book 2 / Book 4 exterior wall elevations for Tower B); NCSTAR 1-1A.

unresolved_relevant.why: NCSTAR 1-1 states only that below floor 7 the columns were combined in groups of three to form single base columns spaced 10 ft on center (pdf p38, pdf p72). No plan dimension for a base column is lettered on Figure 2-3 (pdf p81, which dimensions only the 10 ft grid, the 6'-8" end bay and the 6'-11" corner offset), on Figure 2-8 (pdf p86, which dimensions only tree heights), or on NCSTAR 1-2A Figure 2-6 (pdf p55, column type 6000, elevations only). Without a width the generator cannot draw a base column box, so the base columns are omitted from the model (paradata P-039).

context.what: Buildings inside the study bbox whose recorded construction year is 2001 or earlier, as published today. This is the set that stood in 2001 AND still stands; buildings demolished since 2001 (including the seven World Trade Center buildings) are absent because the source only describes buildings that exist now.

frame.axes: x east, y up, z south (north is -z); same frame as the tower .glb files (paradata P-043)
frame.projection: local equirectangular about the origin: x = (lon - lon0) * cos(lat0) * R * pi / 180, z = -(lat - lat0) * R * pi / 180, R = 6378137 m (WGS84 semi-major axis). Error over a 1 km study area is well under a metre.
frame.y: not carried. ground_elevation_ft is kept per building but not applied; every building is extruded from y = 0 (paradata P-067).
frame.units_in: height_roof_ft and ground_elevation_ft are feet as published; the generator converts with 1 ft = 0.3048 m

origin.method: Area centroid of the quadrilateral whose corners are the junctions of the NYC Street Centerline segments for Church St, Vesey St, Liberty St and West St around the former superblock (the block the six original buildings and the plaza occupied). West St is a divided roadway in CSCL; the junction on its eastern carriageway, the one adjoining the block, is used. Street half-widths were not subtracted: the shift that would make is under 7 ft, and tower positions inside the block are unresolved anyway (paradata P-065, P-066).
origin.cross_check: 0 of 208 filtered footprints have a vertex inside the block quadrilateral

sources.name: Building Footprints (dataset title "BUILDING")
sources.publisher: NYC Office of Technology and Innovation (OTI), via NYC Open Data
notes: height_roof is the height of the CURRENT roof above the building's ground elevation (field documentation: 'The height of the roof above the ground elevation, not height above sea level'). It is not a 2001 measurement; a building altered since 2001 is shown at its present height.

construction_year is 'the year construction of the building was completed', originally from the Department of Finance RPAD file, later from imagery and city systems. Zero or null means unknown; such rows do not pass the filter and are absent.
The dataset contains only buildings that exist today. Buildings demolished after 2001 are not in it, so the context is incomplete by construction: a labeled gap, not an omission the model could fill.
Dataset 5zhs-2jue was republished on the new Socrata backend in 2024 with renamed fields (cnstrct_yr -> construction_year, heightroof -> height_roof, groundelev -> ground_elevation).

context.gap: Only buildings that stood in 2001 and still stand today are shown; neighbours demolished since 2001, and the seven World Trade Center buildings, are absent from the source and therefore from the model. Roof heights are the current roof heights. Massing is unlabeled and carries no names or addresses.
context.material: context_massing: one flat light warm gray shared by every building, a rendering choice so the towers read as the subject
context.nodes: context_NNN, one node and one mesh per building in the data file's order, no identifier carried (P-069: the viewer fades a building that blocks the camera and keeps the eye out of its footprint). All meshes share one POSITION and one NORMAL accessor; each has its own index accessor, so a building's bounds must be computed from its indices.
